title: Largest Number At Least Twice of Others
summary: Given an integer array where the largest number is unique, check if this largest number is at least twice any other number.
statement: Given an integer array where the largest number is unique, check if this largest number is at least twice any other number. Return its index if true, otherwise return -1.
constraints: 1 <= len(nums) <= 50; values are nonnegative and the maximum is unique.
Return the maximum value’s index if it is at least twice every other value, otherwise -1.
reference_solution:
def dominant_index(nums):
    largest=max(range(len(nums)),key=nums.__getitem__)
    second=max((value for index,value in enumerate(nums) if index!=largest),default=0)
    return largest if nums[largest]>=2*second else -1

hints: Only the second-largest value can violate dominance of the maximum.
Find the maximum index and greatest remaining value.
Accept index when maximum >= 2*second; use zero when no second value exists.
If the inequality holds for the second maximum, it holds for every smaller value; otherwise that value is a counterexample.

tests.explanation: Six is at least twice each other value, so its index is one.
Four is not at least twice three, so the answer is -1.
